scope_note: CORRECTED 2026-09-11. An earlier version of this ledger asserted NE@SEA was never forecast. It was: a V1_CANDIDATE forecast was sealed at a T-31h information set and scored against the realised game. BOTH games are genuine prospective case studies, n=2, with different limitations rather than one being unusable.
promotion_rule: No modeling item may be promoted on this evidence. Every MODELING defect below requires multi-game prospective evidence and a pre-registration before any change is scored as an improvement.

defects.symptom: THE PROSPECTIVE LEDGER COULD NOT SEE A SEALED FORECAST THAT EXISTS. nfl/research/shadow/g1_ne_sea/ holds a V1_CANDIDATE forecast sealed before the outcome was opened (bba6f0b) and scored against the realised game (604eaac). Both were committed and both were in the working tree. research.daily_board.discover hard-codes one root (nfl/research/live/) and one label grammar ({pre,post}_inactives_V1_CANDIDATE[_R<n>]); the shadow artifact matched neither, so a review reported its absence as the fact "NE@SEA was NEVER FORECAST". A second seal, g1_ne_sea_runB, was also invisible.
defects.repaired_by: nfl/research/sealed_index.py discovers by CONTENT across every historical namespace; regression test test_sealed_index.py

root_cause_classification.discovery_indexing: YES -- the whole cause. Hard-coded root plus a label grammar the artifact does not match.
root_cause_classification.namespace_migration: CONTRIBUTING -- research/shadow predates research/live and no index spanned both.
root_cause_classification.artifact_retention: NO -- every file present on disk.
root_cause_classification.branch_history: NO -- present in the working tree on this branch.

defects.blast_radius: SYSTEMIC and silent: one of two live games vanished from the evidence base, and every future namespace change would do the same
defects.impact: Severe and second-order. It did not corrupt a number; it corrupted a CONCLUSION, and led to a written claim that was false. Halved the apparent prospective evidence base.
defects.test_required: Done: a historically sealed forecast must remain discoverable when namespaces change (20 checks).

defects.symptom: official_inactives was BLOCKED[NO_EGRESS] for days because capture_vintage.Source never carried content_markers, raising AttributeError in the one executor that could fetch. Once fixed, all ten window captures of /inactives/ were the site placeholder; the list only ever arrived by external delivery.
defects.blast_radius: SYSTEMIC while unrepaired: every game, every week
defects.impact: No official inactive information would have reached any forecast. Repaired, but the generic page still never published, so the external delivery path remains load-bearing.
defects.test_required: Already added: test_source_registry asserts every html source carries the markers it is judged by, with no network. Still needed: an assertion that a capture whose parse yields INACTIVES_PAGE_EMPTY_STATE cannot discharge the obligation.

defects.symptom: Twelve of twelve Sunday clubs filed injury rows with report_status unset, so team_readiness returns INJURY_REPORT_INCOMPLETE and the appearance layer defers.
defects.blast_radius: SYSTEMIC: it is the direct cause of every QB-only board on the slate
defects.impact: Catastrophic for coverage: no RB, WR or TE market is modelled at all for those twelve games. 1012 modelled markets, 0 rankable.
defects.test_required: A capture-time assertion that an injuries capture with report_status unfilled on every row is recorded as INCOMPLETE rather than PASS, plus a slate report of which clubs have filed.

defects.symptom: official_inactive_ids reached the non-QB engine only, so officially inactive quarterbacks kept dropback share: Rourke 0.90 and Simpson 0.73 on the sealed board, with Rourke PEAKING at 22.6% of his team in some draws.
defects.repaired_by: inactive rows zeroed and renormalised before R2/Hamilton, plus a HARD invariant checking the max over draws (622fdd5)
defects.blast_radius: SYSTEMIC: fires for any inactive QB in any game, and the emergency third QB is routinely inactive
defects.impact: Small in the mean (about 2.5% of team dropbacks) but wrong in kind, and the mean hid a 22.6% tail.
defects.test_required: Done: 17 checks including mass conservation to 1e-9. Still needed: a post-repair board for a game with an inactive QB to confirm end to end, which the pregame guard correctly prevented for SF@LA.

defects.symptom: "Enrique Cruz Jr." on the league list did not match "Enrique Cruz" in the roster vintage, and the first run claimed POST_INACTIVES_COMPLETE on 10 of 11 names because resolve() reported an unmapped name rather than refusing.
defects.repaired_by: generational-suffix normalisation, unique match or nothing
defects.blast_radius: RECURRING: any player with a generational suffix
defects.impact: Low on projections here (an offensive lineman, unmodelled) but the overclaim was the real defect.
defects.test_required: Done: a genuine suffix collision still returns AMBIGUOUS.

defects.symptom: One deferred upstream removes FIVE downstream layers at once: carries, targets, receptions, receiving_yards and td_allocation are all absent whenever appearance defers.
defects.impact: The single highest-leverage coverage issue in the system. Fixing D03 or giving appearance a documented degraded mode would restore every non-QB market on a full slate.
defects.test_required: A prospective comparison on >=3 games where a degraded appearance path is scored against the full path, before any degraded mode is allowed to seal.

defects.symptom: layers.appearance compared readiness against INJURIES_READY when the ready state is ENGINE_INPUTS_READY, so the slate-wide path deferred precisely when inputs WERE ready.
defects.blast_radius: Latent: production always names teams and took the other branch, so it never fired in a real run
defects.impact: None observed in production; it masked itself behind a stale test.
defects.test_required: Done: the test now asserts BOTH directions.

defects.symptom: SF@LA: LA ran 57 plays against 65.65 forecast (PIT 0.18, CRPS 5.04) while losing 27-7; SF 64 against 64.50. NE@SEA, now scored from the sealed shadow forecast: NE 42 dropbacks against 33.69 and 31 carries; SEA 27 dropbacks against 30.97 and 22 carries. Both games show the losing or trailing side diverging from forecast volume.
defects.blast_radius: SYSTEMIC: every player market inherits team volume
defects.impact: Large and directional. Stafford -66.6 passing yards is mostly downstream of LA running 8.7 fewer plays than forecast.
defects.test_required: Pre-registered: does conditioning team volume on game state improve CRPS out of sample across >=20 games, with clustering by date and team? Two games cannot answer it.

defects.symptom: The engine has no game-state conditioning at all, so it cannot represent a team trailing by three scores throwing more and running less, or a leading team draining clock.
defects.impact: Both live games show the signature: the losing side in SF@LA under-ran its forecast volume, and both model and market missed the same direction on 6 of 8 markets, which points at environment rather than player share.
defects.test_required: Track 1 pre-registration with a holdout; multi-game evidence required before any promotion.

defects.symptom: Carries were forecast well on both sides (SF 30 actual vs 28.35, LA 29 vs 26.59) while pass volume missed, so the miss is not symmetric across the split.
defects.test_required: Separate the volume miss from the split miss over >=20 games before treating them as different defects.

defects.symptom: The official inactive list moved McCaffrey UP to 13.64 carries when he took 10; his CRPS got WORSE post-inactives (1.48 -> 2.14). Receivers moved correctly (Nacua 64.74 -> 71.00 against 74 actual).
defects.impact: Net information value was only -0.99 CRPS over 10 metrics, about 1%. Redistribution helped receivers and hurt the lead back.
defects.test_required: Does inactive redistribution improve CRPS by position group across >=20 games? One game cannot separate signal from noise.

defects.symptom: Purdy threw 34 times against a 26.71 forecast yet finished with 205 yards against 210.50 -- volume badly under-forecast, yards almost exactly right, so yards-per-attempt was over-forecast by roughly 1.7.
defects.impact: Offsetting errors can look like accuracy; worth watching.
defects.test_required: Decompose yards into attempts x efficiency across >=20 games rather than reading one cancellation.

defects.symptom: Interval coverage was 10/16 at 50%, 16/16 at 80% and 16/16 at 90% on sixteen scored metrics.
defects.impact: Suggestive of intervals being too WIDE at the 80/90 level, but sixteen metrics from one game cannot support that claim, and the metrics are not independent.
defects.test_required: PIT histogram and coverage over >=300 graded metrics with clustering by game, per this project own sample floors.

defects.symptom: No automatic authoritative postgame ingestion exists. SF@LA was scored from an owner-supplied transcription because nflverse had not yet published that game, while NE@SEA pbp WAS available and unused.
defects.impact: Scoring is manual and therefore rare, which is fatal to reaching any of the 300-unit sample floors.
defects.test_required: An automated poll that fetches nflverse pbp when published, hashes it, and scores every sealed board against it with no human step. github.com IS reachable from this executor, so this is buildable now.

defects.symptom: A fresh process pays a fixed ~65s before the first forecast (first game 75.7s, median of the rest 10.7s). slate_fits is 53.9s of it, dominated by appearance_r8.enriched_frame at 51.1s.
defects.blast_radius: Operational only; no effect on any number
defects.impact: A one-game refresh costs 81s instead of ~11s. Incrementality already removes eleven games of work; it cannot remove setup.
defects.test_required: Benchmark C -- warm one-game-changed -- must land near the marginal 10.7s, with a test that shared cached state is immutable or content-hash keyed.

defects.symptom: Nine stored percentiles cannot support exact CRPS; the 1000 stored draws can, and were used. But the pre-inactives boards store draws gzipped and the post ones plain, and the reader had to handle both.
defects.repaired_by: both forms handled; a manifest/array mismatch now returns no vector rather than raising IndexError

defects.symptom: Darnold was forecast 24.48 attempts and threw 2 (PIT 0.066); Lock was forecast 2.10 and threw 22 (PIT 0.981). Darnold was injured early and Lock replaced him. The SEA QB-ROOM AGGREGATE was nearly exact: 200 passing yards actual against 197.46 forecast, 24 attempts against 27.44.
defects.impact: Decisive for how per-QB markets are scored. The room aggregate was forecastable and was forecast well; the split was not knowable from any pregame information set. Scoring per-QB markets without separating these will keep charging irreducible in-game variance to the model.
defects.test_required: Score the QB-ROOM AGGREGATE alongside the per-QB split on every game, and report them apart. Before any allocation change, show across >=20 games that per-QB CRPS is improvable at all given that mid-game replacement is unobservable pregame.

defects.symptom: NE: 42 dropbacks against 33.69 forecast (+8.31) but 178 passing yards against 212.46 (-34.46). SF@LA: Purdy 34 attempts against 26.71 but 205 yards against 210.50. In both games the team that threw more than forecast gained fewer yards per attempt than forecast.
defects.impact: Offsetting errors make yardage look accurate while both components are wrong. If real, it is a volume/efficiency coupling the model lacks.
defects.test_required: Decompose yards into attempts x efficiency and test the coupling across >=20 games. TWO GAMES IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING.

ne_sea_limitations: information set T-31h (newest observation 2026-09-08T17:06:03Z against a 2026-09-10T00:20:00Z kickoff), NOT T-90m
no official inactives existed at seal time
no player-level receiving or rushing forecast was produced
C3 not reached; components applied were A1, A3G, C0, R2, SC1
many rows carry NO_FORECAST_MISSING_PREGAME_INPUT and are scored as such
comparability_note: NE@SEA and SF@LA are comparable ONLY on team volume and QB quantities. SF@LA carries receiving and rushing layers that NE@SEA never produced, and the two information sets differ by ~30 hours, so any difference between them confounds architecture, cutoff and opponent.
